# Model card: synthetic_bd

*Synthetic demo data. Decision support only.* Written by `python -m src.model.model_card` from the reports; do not edit by hand.

**Model version:** `synthetic_bd-20261015-005409-9db9d66`

## Intended use

Decision support for credit officers: a repayment score with its coverage, band and plain reasons, shown next to the merchant's records. The officer decides and records why. Not for automatic approval or decline.

## Data

- **Source:** Synthetic merchants generated by our own code. Monthly seasonality follows Bangladesh Bank's mobile-money merchant payments. The repayment share (90%) is a team assumption, set between published Bangladesh recovery rates and early-default rates in other Asian data; the other proportions are team assumptions too (config/default.yaml).
- **Terms:** Our own data; no third-party terms.
- **Outcome (label):** Repaid in time: the loan was paid in full no more than 30 days after its due date.
- **Split:** Split by loan issue date. Each period ends the day before the next begins.
- **Loans:** 13,318 to train, 5,853 to measure (validation). The held-back test loans are not used here.

## Model

- **Model in use:** logistic regression, calibration: none (the model's probabilities were already well calibrated).
- **Why this model:** LightGBM adds +0.0128 AUC over the logistic regression (range +0.0032 to +0.0212; the whole range must reach +0.0100). Not met: whole gain range reaches the threshold. (The simpler model stays unless the other is clearly better.)
- **Inputs** (each can only push the score the way its meaning says; how much data exists about a borrower is never an input):
  - Purchase value last 90 days vs the 90 before, %
  - Chance that two of the merchant's purchases in the last 90 days came from the same supplier (counted over all pairs of purchases, so it does not depend on how many purchases there were)
  - Mean days late over past payments
  - Payments over 7 days late, 90 days
  - Share of payments within 3 days of due
  - Used limit / limit
  - Merchant-attributable returns (refused, wrong item) / total, 90 days; address and rider returns left out when the reason is recorded
  - Failed parcels not tagged as an address or rider problem / total, 90 days
  - Share of cash-on-delivery money passed back on time
  - Median hours from dispatch to delivery

## Results (validation period)

| Measure | Value | 95% range |
|---|---|---|
| AUC (0.50 = coin toss; about 0.70 is useful) | 0.710 | 0.688 to 0.729 |
| Brier score (always-average: 0.087) | 0.082 | 0.077 to 0.088 |
| Calibration error | 0.012 | 0.010 to 0.021 |
| Simpler model (purchases only: what a platform knows before any credit or delivery history) AUC | 0.667 | |
| What the full model adds | 0.043 | 0.028 to 0.060 |

| Band | Share of loans | Repaid |
|---|---|---|
| Strong | 56% | 95.2% |
| Review | 29% | 82.1% |
| Needs more info | 15% | 88.3% |

**What this shows.** The whole pipeline runs and behaves as designed: time split, two candidate models, calibration, bands, reasons, and a negative control (delivery inputs add nothing when the generator gives them no signal).

**What this does not show.** How accurate the tool would be for real merchants. The data is generated by our own code.

## Results on the held-back test period

| Measure | Validation | Test | Test 95% range |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUC | 0.710 | 0.728 | 0.707 to 0.749 |
| Brier score | 0.082 | 0.082 | 0.076 to 0.088 |
| Calibration error | 0.012 | 0.008 | 0.007 to 0.018 |

6,023 test loans, 90.2% repaid. Brier score of always predicting the training average on them: 0.088. Test bands: strong 55%, review 29%, needs more info 16%. The model, its calibration and the band lines were fixed before this look and were not changed after it.

**Reading.** Not a clean holdout: while the generator's noise was tuned in Phase 1, and once in a later audit probe, a rough model was scored on these test months (see the earlier uses below). The result agrees with validation, but it is no stronger evidence than the validation result.

The ledger `reports/<mode>/test_set_use.json` has 3 entries for this test period (one entry can cover several looks; its detail says). Earlier uses: generator difficulty check (Phase 1, Oct 12-13); audit probes (Oct 13).

## Ablation (synthetic data; does each data source add anything?)

| Delivery signal strength | Deliveries add (mean over seeds) | Lowest | Highest |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | +0.0000 | -0.0003 | +0.0004 |
| 0.5 | +0.0250 | +0.0229 | +0.0275 |
| 1 | +0.0551 | +0.0527 | +0.0568 |

At strength 0 the generator gives deliveries no link to repayment, so they must add nothing; they do not. Details: `reports/ablation/ABLATION.md`.

## Group audit (validation period)

- No group gap was flagged in any of 3 seeds on these data.
- Each group is compared with everyone else, so a gap in one group also shows, mirrored, in the other groups of the same column.
- Columns audited: town tier, shop type, trade licence. Full table: `reports/FAIRNESS.md`.

## Limits

- All results use synthetic data. They show that the pipeline is sound, not that the model is accurate on ShopUp merchants.
- The delivery (REDX) signal is a hypothesis tested by ablation, including a zero-signal control. It is not an established predictor of repayment.
- The periods follow each other with no gap. The outcome of a loan issued near the end of one period became known only after the next period began, but training (and the calibration) used it as if it had been known. A strict forward test would leave a gap; without it the results are a little optimistic.
- Labels exist only for people who received credit before. The model may not work for applicants who would have been turned down under earlier policy.
- Scores are less certain when coverage is low. A thin file is never treated as a bad file: below the coverage line the band is 'Needs more info', whatever the score.
- The validation numbers are a little optimistic: that period was also used to choose the model and the calibration. The held-back test period gives the honest check.
- Group columns are used only to audit results, never as model inputs. The group audit shows where the model works measurably differently on these data; it does not show that the model is fair.
- The tool supports a human decision. It must not be used for automatic approval or decline.
